## Overview

You have been writing R code in
[Quarto {{< fa external-link >}}](https://quarto.org/){target="_blank"}
documents since week 12.
This week, we will take a closer look at Quarto documents:
we will see more options to **customize** your documents
and to show or hide code and figures,
and what happens when you render a document.
We will also see how to **structure** your documents,
and how to record the R and package versions you used.

There is only one class this week, on Monday, because of the Thanksgiving break.

## Learning goals

Some of the things you will learn this week:

#### [Quarto and reproducible R workflows](./w14a_quarto.qmd)

- What happens when Quarto renders a document
- More about **YAML** syntax and useful options in the YAML header
- How to use **chunk options**, including for figures, and how to set them for a whole document
- How to include R output in your Markdown text
- How to structure a Quarto document,
  and how to write file paths that also work when rendering (with the _here_ package)
- How to record the versions of R and R packages that you used
- How to render a document to Markdown that displays well on GitHub

## Assignments and exercises

- **Final Project**: [Progress report](/FP/FP2.qmd) [_(Due 11/29)_]{style="color:#bb0000"}
- There is no exercise page this week:
  you'll practice with this week's Quarto material in the
  [week 15 exercises](/week15/w15_exercises.qmd).

## Optional self-study material

- [Additional Quarto material](/bonus/quarto.qmd):
  chunk labels, Positron's visual editor and inline chunk output,
  how to cite papers and software, how to cache slow code chunks,
  and how to turn an R script into a Quarto document
- [R package environments with _renv_](/bonus/renv.qmd):
  how to give each project its own package library,
  and record and restore package versions
